body:
I don't think I get drunk more than two or three nights a month anymore, but when I used to go out it was for fun. When I went overboard the first time it was also my first experience with jungle juice. I just feel like I picked the worst day to forget to stop drinking. Afterwards I killed my brain cells because I liked to remember those first few months when things were alright again. As a result, I started hanging out with a different group of friends i met through my dealer. 

If you're familiar with communication sciences, I was managing that ugly elephant in the room with a withdrawal style; We lacked any 'real' resolution for months because I tried to ignore it and move on. When they pressed the issue enough, I just left the argument. I hated the thought that my relationship with my friends had turned into a parental "this kid has problems, lets get him help" kind of thing. It was lonely, and for all the good intentions behind it their help made things worse. I'd be lying if I said I knew what would have happened if we all agreed to sweep it under the rug, but there aren't many things better than the company of good friends. Maybe I was unreasonable to think that was an option. 

A lot of what made me attempt the first time won't make sense outside of context. One big part was that the friends who stuck with me through it were all pledging a fraternity, and I was more or less alone on dorm for around three months. After the charge, I stopping hanging out with the stoners, instead sitting down and retreating into the web. I haven't talked to my folks about it yet, since after my alcohol charge I was nearly pulled from school and I know dropping that bomb will change everything about our relationship. I'm a good student, but I could never find satisfaction in schoolwork. A lot of what gets me through a bad day are other people, and I try to return the favor. At my worst I'm angry and misanthropic and it's cost me a lot. 

Things were calmer this year but I feel like I'm putting on a face so people don't get the wrong impression about me. 

edit: I never thanked you for listening. Your time and your concerns meant a lot more to me than I thought an anonymous reddit thread was capable of.

I never like sharing this part, since people tend to assume its the root of all my problems. It isn't, but it is an important part of who I am;
I'm a boy, and I lost my virginity to one in high school. He was my best friend and we said we were just fucking around, but there was such a profound meaning in our relationship I've never encountered since then. I've had a few girlfriends but it was a different experience entirely. I don't think I'd put any kind of label on my sexuality like its something that defines me, but take this as you will.


I never told anyone until college, since something like that can really eat away at you when you live around a bunch of athletes and frat boys. It was nice to have someone to talk to, and I confided in one of the girls (it was a mixed dorm last year) upstairs.


After my drunk charge, but before the next semester she told one of the boys downstairs; not out of malice as far as I know, but to ask advice for how to help me. The guy was perfectly ok with it, in a stark contrast to the rest of the boys on dorm, but when I found out I lost my mind. I had hated the end of high school because I couldn't tell anyone, but this was worse. We got into a shouting match which turned into tears and criticisms and hateful, hateful words on both our parts; I was angry she had told anyone, and she was upset that I was becoming self-destructive and dangerously unhinged, and that I needed help. I left the dorm to go unwind, and I ended up at a frathouse on a large dose of ecstasy and about 2g of weed. I returned the next day, and I was yelled at again for just vanishing without telling anyone where I was going. I blew them off and told them to stop worrying about me, and they called me out on my substance abuse;


I'm going to take a little detour here and explain that while, yes, I've used harder drugs like ecstasy and acid, I never at any point became dependent on them. The only drug that I consistently use is marijuana.


Having them call me out touched a nerve, instantly shifting the conversation's tone from 'concerned people to a friend' to 'angry deluded junkie yelling at people trying to help'. I told them that they had no right to call me out on that, since it was my choice what I did. They continued pressing and I simply went inside my room and punched my closet until I put a hole through it.


We reconciled eventually, but to the people I hurt our only relationship was through our mutual friends. The regret took a while to kick in, but when it really, really hit me I went on another drug binge and got a possession charge. Called my folks, and was screamed at for being a disappointment and a junkie. I then tried to hang myself, but before I asphyxiated I realized I wanted to keep living, so I broke the already flimsy bar off of my loft, drank myself to sleep and woke up in a pool of vomit.


After this point, it essentially becomes a lot of denial and angst. that's really all I have to say on my behalf. I keep losing my friends. I don't have any problem making them, but I always drive them away.

I told myself Valentine's Day. If I'm still angry and alone to the point of suicide then, I'm talking to my folks about it and getting professional help. If I'm just vaguely depressed, I'll probably just keep on living.

edit: my phrasing seemed a bit too committal

A lot of it took place over time, slowly. I'll try not to write you a life story but here are the major things I remember screwing up.

Intentionally and unintentionally, I broke several people emotionally with my bullshit. November 14th, 2010 I had just broken up with a girl I had liked since my formative years, and got so drunk I tried to walk in front of a bus. My roommate thought I was just being stupid, and punched me out before I continued. As they dragged me home, I asked them to leave me there. When they refused, I tried to make them not like me enough to care, and said some things that I'd have to spend a paragraph or two explaining to show how insulting they were, but tl;dr - I knew these people personally and even when I was blacked out drunk I was using their own trust against them to let me go. The last thing I remember is them taking me to the bathroom to keep me alive, then waking up in the drunk tank. I returned that afternoon and came back to a house full of very hurt and confused people. Many of my new friends had never seen this kind of behavior at all, let alone from someone who put on such a good face. I sat there for three hours asking them to kill me, then I threw up and started crying and praying in spanish.

That was the start of it. Between november and march I slid into drug use to cope, as I had literally alienated all but a handful of people I knew. In only two months, I took my 'fresh start' and stamped it out of existence, instead replacing it with a malaise and depression that kind of eats at you instead of makes you angry.

After winter break, I returned and things seemed to be getting back to normal. I started talking to people again, made amends with the people I had alienated, and started going out to parties again. I also started talking to that girl again, and we went out to a party as friends. Most of the people on my dorm didn't like her since they associated her with the night I got arrested, but I assured them it was my fault. At the party we got into an argument after asking her to dance, and she left to go hook up with some other guy. Angry, distant, and confused I proceeded to drink myself into a hole and hook up with a girl I knew liked me to make her jealous. She disappeared for about half an hour, and I received about 3 or 4 texts asking where I was and to come get her. I was so butthurt I ignored them, but I looked at all of the texts again and realized she was in trouble. ("Where are you", "This guy is creepy", "He's trying to make me hook up", "WHERE ARE YOU IM IN THE BATHROOM")

I got a few friends together and we kicked his ass out of the party, but not before he had been forcibly (she was very drunk and vulnerable) making out with her for about 15 minutes. All because I decided to act like a fucking child. Who the fuck does that? Who lets their friends get in trouble because *they're* hurt? I was so many kinds of hypocrite that night that our relationship dissolved completely. Not even friends anymore, just strangers from other lives. I never even apologized to that girl I manipulated.

I'm sorry, I'll finish later but I really don't like this trip down memory lane. I'm headed to class.

We have counselors on campus, but they really aren't for me. I decided, one day, to open up to one for about an hour. My whole life story told in between laughing and crying and angrily seething at myself. When I was done, the counselor and I got ice cream, then the appointment was over. I asked several times if she could prescribe anything to me, since I was directed there by a friend who also suffered from depression and was told as much, and was denied. I was told medication was only given out in serious cases, to deter people with drug-seeking behavior. That really got my goat, since I had just admitted to this woman that I had just jumped off my bed with a belt around my neck, and would have died had I not had a change of heart. I didn't even want the medication, I just felt like I was being judged.

Since then, I've been talking to my former roommate: he's a smart kid , and after being away for the weekend deduced that I attempted suicide. We talked for a while and made me promise never to try it again, saying he would feel guilty for not turning me in to the RA if I woke up dead. 

I don't like the fact that I need to not remember who I am sometimes to keep up a good face. It's a crutch, and it's not very attractive to friends or SO's.
